links.outcome: Balanced accuracy after fine-tuning on new-centre data vs direct out-of-distribution testing
links.effect: Out-of-distribution application reduced balanced accuracy by 6.5% to 16.0%; fine-tuning via transfer learning ameliorated this reduction. Retraining from scratch gave equivalent performance but took much longer.
links.quote: This reduction can be ameliorated through fine-tuning the network on the new database through transfer learning.

links.effect: Balanced accuracy fell by 6.5% to 16.0% when networks were applied out-of-distribution.
links.quote: Each network shows significantly reduced performance (on the order of a 6.5% to 16.0% reduction in balanced accuracy) when applied out-of-distribution.

links.effect: Domain shift across databases and centres reduced balanced accuracy by 6.5% to 16.0% out-of-distribution.
links.quote: Each network shows significantly reduced performance (on the order of a 6.5% to 16.0% reduction in balanced accuracy) when applied out-of-distribution.

links.effect: Fine-tuning ameliorated the 6.5% to 16.0% out-of-distribution balanced-accuracy reduction.
links.quote: This reduction can be ameliorated through fine-tuning the network on the new database through transfer learning.

links.effect: Across three databases from two centres with differing hardware/protocols, out-of-distribution balanced accuracy fell by 6.5% to 16.0%.
links.quote: Each network shows significantly reduced performance (on the order of a 6.5% to 16.0% reduction in balanced accuracy) when applied out-of-distribution.

links.effect: MER classifiers were negatively affected by domain shift; OOD balanced accuracy fell by 6.5% to 16.0%.
links.quote: We have demonstrated that a variety of recent machine learning algorithms for MER classification are negatively affected by domain shift, but that this can be quickly ameliorated through simple transfer learning procedures that can be readily performed for new centres.
